lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Everyone says the Nazca Lines were drawn to be seen from the sky.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: A machine just found three hundred and three that weren't.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: In Peru's southern desert, people scraped away dark stones to draw a hummingbird, a monkey, a spider, some longer than three football fields.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Who said they were for the sky? Pilots helped make them famous.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: But in nineteen twenty-seven, Toribio Mejía found them on foot, hiking the foothills.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: For nearly a century, researchers counted about four hundred and thirty figures.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Then a Japanese team gave aerial photos to an I B M artificial intelligence.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: In six months it led them to three hundred and three new ones. Nearly doubling the count.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Smaller. Older. Drawn beside walking trails, to be seen by people passing on foot.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: Humans, llamas, and killer whales holding knives.

lines.speaker: d
lines.text: So who were the giant ones for? Nobody explained it.
